data.title: Covalent Molecular Architecture
data.description: Master covalent bonding, valence rules, and Lewis structures by building complex chemical molecules.

targetMolecule.name: Ethanol
targetMolecule.realWorldUse: Ethanol is the active antimicrobial agent in hand sanitizers and is widely used as a renewable fuel source.
targetMolecule.imagePrompt: A clear bottle of hand sanitizer gel sitting on a laboratory desk with scientific diagrams of covalent bonds glowing in the background.

challenges.instruction: Examine this built covalent molecule containing one carbon and four hydrogen atoms. What is its name?
challenges.hint: It is the primary component of natural gas.
challenges.narration: Spot on! Methane (CH4) is a simple alkane with tetrahedral geometry.

challenges.instruction: Write the formula for this molecule.
challenges.hint: Count the atoms of each element in the drawing.
challenges.narration: Excellent chemistry writing! H2SO4 is one of the most widely produced industrial chemicals in the world.

challenges.instruction: How many covalent bonds does a nitrogen atom typically form to complete its octet?
challenges.hint: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons and needs 3 more to reach 8.
challenges.narration: Correct! Nitrogen forms three covalent bonds, often seen in ammonia (NH3) and nitrogen gas (N2).

challenges.instruction: Build a molecule of Ammonia using one nitrogen and three hydrogen atoms.
challenges.hint: Connect each hydrogen atom with a single bond to the central nitrogen atom.
challenges.narration: Brilliant! You built Ammonia (NH3), a vital compound used in fertilizers and household cleaners.

challenges.instruction: Predict the molecular geometry of carbon dioxide (CO2), which features double bonds between carbon and each oxygen atom.
challenges.hint: When double bonds push away from each other on opposite sides of a central atom, what shape do they form?
challenges.narration: Fantastic! Carbon dioxide adopts a linear molecular geometry due to repulsion between its double bond electron domains.
